newsitem.title: INDIA: INDIAN HEADLINE STOCKS - factors to watch - Oct 28.
newsitem.headline: INDIAN HEADLINE STOCKS - factors to watch - Oct 28.

text.p: Following are some of the main factors affecting Indian stock markets on Monday morning:

** Prime Minister H D Deve Gowda on Sunday announced a 61 billion rupee political and economic package for the North-Eastern states aimed at strengthening the infrastructural sectors, especially power, communication, railways and agriculture, the Times of India reports

** A five-day old strike which has crippled India's phone and postal services will continue until the government gives trade unions a written assurance to meet workers' demands, trade union officials said on Sunday
** The Union Minister of State for Petroleum, T R Balu has ruled out any upward revision in the price of petroleum products, the Financial Express says
** Indian blue-chip stocks are likely to revive the rally sparked by lower interest rates and notch further gains this week, but the undercurrent is suspect, brokers and analysts said at the weekend
The benchmark Bombay Stock Exchange 30-share index rose 120.45 points or 3.8 percent to end at 3,250.66 on Friday -- after a 6.7 percent rise in two straight days triggered profit-taking last week

** The Arvind Mafatlal group is hiving off the petrochemicals business of the 12 billion rupee NOCIL into a separate joint venture with a foreign partner holding a majority stake, the Business Standard reports
** US Conglomerate Intel has entered into a strategic alliance with the 4 billion rupee Padmini Polymers, the Economic Times reports
Through this agreement, both Intel and Padmini Polymers (through its group company Padmini Multimedia) will compliment and promote each other's products in the field of multimedia, the paper says
